correctness.rationale: Exact support formula follows from the orthogonal support of each hyperdisk. The S² conditional angular measure gives the derivative of the three-coordinate survival function, and its antiderivative gives the CDF with correct normalization at both ends. The fixed-d lower edge is the Dirichlet density evaluated at its barycenter times the exactly computed simplex volume; the upper edge is a first-order union expansion with two-coordinate intersections O(t²). Gaussian minima and radial LLN imply the d³ exponential-square limit. The actual packaged verify_width.py ran successfully. Monte Carlo and finite disk samples corroborate but do not prove unbounded-dimensional claims.

value.rationale: The 3D full width distribution is a natural exact anisotropy invariant of the convex hull of three orthogonal equal disks, tied canonically to the Euclidean 2-support norm ball. The sharp lower and upper endpoint exponents and constants have geometric interpretations as near-equidistributed coordinate directions versus near-coordinate-hyperplane directions; the high-d rescaling identifies the typical microscopic width deficit. They solve a complete natural distribution problem rather than an arbitrary finite exercise, and are not supplied by known means, radii, volumes, or the generic norm representation.
